summary: RETEST iter 14 — LanguageSwitcher HIGH bug (from iter 13) is RESOLVED. The onClick now calls window.history.replaceState to sync URL ?lang= with the selected language BEFORE the soft reload, so detectInitial() reads the correct value on hydration. Verified end-to-end via Playwright: 7/7 sub-tests PASS (FR initial load, switcher menu open, FR→EN switch, EN→NL switch, document.documentElement.lang updates, localStorage-only NL regression with no URL param). No backend retesting required (21/21 from iter 13 already green).

issues: Auth/CTA buttons 'Entrar' and 'Suscribirse' remain in Spanish on /?lang=fr|en|nl pages. They appear to be hardcoded strings in the header instead of using the t('nav.signin') / t('nav.subscribe') keys (which already exist in DICT for es/en/fr/nl). LOW priority — does not block the i18n flow, but visually inconsistent next to translated nav (Home/Trends/Topics...).
Console shows 2× '401 Unauthorized' per page load (likely /api/me probe for anon user). Cosmetic, not a regression.

action_items: (Optional, LOW) Wire the header 'Entrar' / 'Suscribirse' buttons to t('nav.signin') and t('nav.subscribe') so they switch with the rest of the nav. Keys are already present in DICT for all 4 languages.
(Optional) Silence the anonymous /api/me 401 console noise by returning {user:null} 200 when no session cookie, or catching the 401 client-side.
critical_code_review_comments: LanguageSwitcher.jsx (lines 48-61) fix is correct and minimal: history.replaceState updates URL ?lang= synchronously inside a try/catch before the setTimeout(reload, 80). detectInitial() in i18n.js (URL > localStorage > navigator) now reads the just-set value, ending the previous override loop.
i18n.js detectInitial precedence (URL first) remains semantically correct (shareable links with ?lang=xx should win); the switcher just had to keep the URL in sync — fixed.

Hero h1 now correctly renders dynamic Claude translation in NL ('Ontdek de waarheid voordat het algoritme deze verstoort.') confirming the dynamic translateOnDemand + cache pipeline still works post-fix.

Soft reload approach (window.location.reload after URL rewrite) is acceptable but heavyweight. A future improvement: drop the reload and trigger re-render via setLangState + cache invalidation, since api.js interceptor already injects lang on every request. Would shave ~1.5s off every language switch.
